automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Public sources must display an unambiguous publication or update date within the prior seven days; missing, ambiguous, future-dated, and strict-boundary-only dates are excluded.

federation_note: GitHub, Copilot, CodeQL, GitHub Agentic Workflows, Descope, WebMCP, and MCP server/product background remain upstream-owned. This raw artifact retains only downstream operating implications for AI-assisted development practice.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub made AI Scan for pull requests generally available. It reports AI-labelled advisory findings beside CodeQL findings when enabled, may suggest an autofix, does not fail the code-scanning check or block merges through rulesets, and has stated scope and credit-use boundaries.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/adoption-and-operating-model/h: Treat AI security findings as review inputs with explicit disposition and merge-authority boundaries rather than autonomous acceptance criteria.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/ai-assiste: Keep advisory findings, coverage exclusions, budget ownership, and the independent acceptance gate visible in the repair record.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Ingest only the local practice rule: an AI scan is advisory unless separately backed by a deterministic required check and explicit policy.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced general availability of agentic autofix for code-scanning alerts. The flow explores relevant files, proposes and validates a fix by rerunning CodeQL, then opens a draft pull request with rationale and validation steps; enterprise policy enablement, repository or organization enablement, billing, and cost controls apply.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/adoption-and-operating-model/h: A draft pull request and tool rerun support review; neither replaces explicit human acceptance authority.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/agent-workflows/agent-control-: Controlled remediation can use a bounded explore-propose-validate-draft sequence with a separate review transition.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/ai-proces: Persist alert scope, enablement state, validation output, draft status, and reviewer decision as workflow state rather than transient agent context.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/applicati: A repair harness should make policy enablement, scoped evidence, validation, cost budget, and reviewable output explicit components.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/ai-assiste: A security repair gate needs evidence from the original alert, remediation rationale, rerun output, and independent review before merge.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Keep product mechanics upstream; ingest the downstream controlled-remediation checklist only if it adds a reusable local gate.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub announced a public preview of workflow dependency lockfiles. Lockfiles pin Actions and reusable-workflow dependencies to reviewed commits, support gradual onboarding and stale-lockfile checks, and can be required by administrators; dependency safety still requires review.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/ai-assiste: Agent-driven repair and validation workflows should pin and review their execution dependencies, while retaining a separate safety review for the dependencies themselves.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Consider a local rule requiring reproducible, reviewable CI dependencies for agent-driven repair workflows.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: GitHub Agentic Workflows published an example daily documentation updater that reviews merged work and opens a reviewable pull request through a safe output. Its reported runs distinguish one successful execution from two early infrastructure failures before the agent began, with recorded costs and failure location.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/application-patterns/declarati: Declare reviewable output, run outcome, activation failure, and evidence links as workflow artifacts so an automation can be audited and resumed.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/automated-upd: An update feed should expose a reviewable change boundary and distinguish collector failure from an absence of source changes.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/clipping-and-: Raw intake should preserve source-to-artifact traceability and run status before any downstream synthesis.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/source-workflows/leaf-update-w: The ledger should record failed-before-scan runs separately from completed scans with no qualifying updates.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Treat this as an implementation example, not a generic reliability claim; retain the local observability and review-boundary implications.

qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Descope announced Agentic Identity Hub 3.0 with an approval-based onboarding workflow, documented purpose and owner, least-privilege access, MCP gateway controls, short-lived or workload identity options, request-time policy evaluation, and audit logging. These are vendor claims in a product announcement.

why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/governance-and-risk/agent-iden: The local control checklist should connect a named owner, purpose, scoped authority, revocation path, and audit record rather than rely on shared long-lived credentials.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/retrieval-and-tools/remote-mcp: Discovery and onboarding of remote skills should be separated from runtime authorization and monitored access.
why_it_matters_for_leaves.docs/wiki/retrieval-and-tools/tool-call-: Tool governance can require identity-aware, request-time policy evaluation and auditable access decisions for each invocation.

qualifying_updates.follow_up_note: Do not promote vendor claims into universal facts; use the announcement only to test whether local ownership, authority, and audit requirements are complete.

excluded_candidates.reason: The page visibly changed in-window, but does not identify a substantive October change; its underlying workflow claims are already represented in earlier sources, so this run does not infer a new durable update.
Future-dated relative to this run (October 16 local time); excluded rather than treating it as an in-window update.

The candidate is primarily broad WebMCP protocol and browser-product background, which federation assigns upstream; it provides no distinct downstream local-practice change for the selected RAG or MCP leaves.
